description: 1 Dough, 4 Cookie Flavors! Base Brown Butter Cookie Dough: 113 g unsalted butter (1/2 cup) melted 100 g brown sugar (1/2 cup) 50 g granulated sugar (1/4 cup) 1 tsp vanilla extract 1 large egg room temp. 156 g all-purpose flour (1 1/4 cups) 1/2 tsp baking soda 1/4 tsp salt 15 g milk powder (1 tbsp) 100-130 g semi-sweet chocolate chunks/chips Mix-ins: Dark chocolate chunks  White chocolate chunks  Chocolate chips (optional) Crushed Biscoff cookies  Biscoff spread Crushed oreos Cocoa powder  Milk  Instructions  Spoon 1 heaping tsp each of biscoff  spread onto a lined tray (I made 4 dollops) and place in the freezer while you make the dough. Brown the butter over medium heat until golden and nutty (~5 minutes). Transfer to a bowl and let cool for 15 minutes. Whisk in the brown sugar, granulated sugar, egg, and vanilla until smooth. Add the flour, baking soda, milk powder, and salt,  then fold everything together until just combined. Divide the dough into 4 separate bowls. Into the first bowl add dark chocolate chunks and mix to combine. This is the chocolate chip cookie dough. Scoop and place on a lined tray. In the second bowl, add add 2 tsp of cocoa powder and 1/2 tbsp of milk. Mix until combined, if the dough is too dry (not the original consistency) add another 1/2 tbsp of milk. Then mix in dark chocolate chunks and this is your double chocolate chip cookie dough. Scoop and place on a lined tray. In the third bowl add crushed biscoff cookies and white chocolate chunks, mix to combine. Scoop and place on a lined tray. Flatten each of the cookie dough balls on the palm of you hand and place a frozen biscoff spread dollop in the center, cover it with cookie and roll until smooth. Repeat with the rest of the biscoff cookie dough balls. In the third bowl add crushed oreo cookies , white chocolate chunks and chocolate chips (optional). Mix until combined. Scoop and place on a lined tray. Add more toppings on the scooped cookie dough balls, chill for 30 min. Bake in an oven preheated to 180°C (350°F) for 12-14 min. Once baked, let cool on the tray for 5 min, before transferring on a cooling rack to cool completely. Enjoy!  . . . . . #fyp #cookies #trending #chocolatechipcookies #food
transcript: One dough for irresistible flavors. Did you know chocolate chip cookies were invented in 1938 by Ruth Wakefield who was making butter cookies and added chocolate pieces expecting them to melt into the dough. Instead they held their shape and thus creating the iconic chocolate chip cookies. It became so popular in fact that she made a deal with Nestle in exchange for the right to use her recipe on their packaging. She was given a lifetime supply of chocolate. Honestly that's so valid. I too would do anything for a lifetime supply of chocolate. Now there's tons of flavors of cookies and if you want to have them all without all the effort this is a recipe to make four different flavors with one base brown butter cookie dough flavors are the classic chocolate chip double chocolate chip for those of you who are obsessed with chocolate like me bisque off white chocolate for those of you who want a little bit of a rich indulgent treat and finally cookies and cream because what is better than crushed Oreos and white chocolate in a gooey cookie. One tip I have for you is to add on more toppings on each of the cookie dough balls before baking that we can tell what flavor each cookie is just by looking at it even though it is kind of obvious but you know what I mean they just look much prettier like that. I actually make these cookies for a gift I wanted to do something that was easy to transport and package without any frosting and I think it turned out so cute these different cookies stacked on top of each other. I will leave the detailed recipe in the description box below.
